2. The facts giving rise to this Rule are that the plaintiff petitioners instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 53 of 1990 against the defendant opposite parties for a declaration of their title to the suit land described in the schedule to the plaint and for a further declaration that the order passed in Mutation Case No. 96/81-82 is illegal, collusive and not binding upon the plaintiff petitioners and also for a direction to the defendants to hand over possession of the suit land to the plaintiffs. The case of the plaintiffs, as it appears by a reading of this application and the counter affidavit of the defendant opposite parties and the impugned judgment of the learned District Judge, is that the plaintiffs became owner of the suit land by purchase on the basis of registered kabalas but that the defendant No. 1 was trying to lease out the suit land to some other persons and then the plaintiffs filed a non GR Case No. 11 of 1983 under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure wherein the property was attached and a receiver was appointed by the learned Magistrate under section 146 CrPC. Thereafter, the plaintiffs filed the above mentioned Title Suit No. 53 of 1990 against the defendants. The defendant opposite parties contested the suit by filing a written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint. The defendants case as it appears from the counter affidavits is that the suit land was the excess khash land of the Shariatulla Waqf Estate which on being surrendered under the provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act vested in the Government and the record of rights was prepared in the name of the Government and that the plaintiffs' documents of purchase are collusive ones and not according to the provisions of law. 

 9. Mr. Moazzam Hossain, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the defendant appellant opposite parties, has argued that the ex parte judgment passed by the learned Subordinate Judge in Title Suit No. 53 of 1990 does not conform to the provision of law in view of the fact that the learned Subordinate Judge did not state in the judgment properly as to how the plaintiffs suit was proved. In this connection, the learned Deputy Attorney-General referred to a decision in the case of Bangladesh Vs. Israil and others reported in 1981 BLD (AD) 371 wherein it has been held that the court to observe minimum legal requirements, judgment should show application of Court's judicial mind as to whether the plaintiffs witnesses and the papers produced proved the plaintiffs case. The learned Deputy Attorney Attorney-General said that the learned Subordinate Judge did not apply his judicial mind before coming to the conclusion that the plaintiffs have approved their case and therefore, the judgment of the learned Subordinate Judge being not in conformity with the minimum requirement of law, the learned District Judge is justified in appointing the receiver by his impugned judgment and order dated 19.11.92 till the hearing of the appeal. 

 14. By a perusal of the impugned order of the learned District Judge dated 19.11.92, it appears that the plaintiff petitioners started non-GR Case No. 11 of 1983 in which the property in dispute was kept under attachment and then the learned Magistrate appointed a receiver for the management of the property and that the plaintiffs' mutation case No. 96/81-82 was also rejected. From this fact it appears that the plaintiffs were not in possession of the suit land since after their purchase till the date of disposal of the Title Suit No. 53 of 1990 and that the plaintiffs did not try to prove their possession under section 145 CrPC in the court of the learned Magistrate. Further, it appears from the impugned order of the learned District Judge that the learned Subordinate Judge did not state in her ex parte order how she came to the finding that the plaintiffs have proved their case. On the other hand, it appears that the learned GP after deposition of the PW 1 had appeared and prayed for cross examination of the PW 1 but that the learned Subordinate Judge did not allow the prayer of the learned GP. The learned District Judge on this point observed that the learned Subordinate Judge being over zealous has inquired into the reasons whether the learned GP actually was engaged in other courts as stated in his petition and then she rejected the prayer of the learned GP. Further, it appears from the impugned order that the learned District Judge observed that the plaintiffs did not enter into physical possession of the suit land although they stated that they were trying to grow boro paddy in the suit land and under such circumstances the learned District Judge came to the finding that in such view of the matter, appointment of a receiver will meet the ends of justice in this case. 

 16. For the reasons stated above, we find nothing to interfere with the impugned order of the learned District Judge.
